page0.text:
She dashes down the corridor, chasing the skull mask.
The distance between them closes from 18 meters to a mere five.
Saber is close enough to cleave her enemy in two with a single step.

page1.text:
But the enemy knows that, too.
If she closes in, he throws daggers to prevent her from finishing the fight, and if she doesn't close in, that gives him a chance to retreat.

page2.text:
The skull doesn't sprint with galelike speed the way Saber does, but retreats with bestial agility.
He slips through the narrow corridors with ease, navigating tight turns without losing speed.
Does he have eyes in the back of his head, or is his back the mask he turns towards Saber when he faces her down?
Assassin, the skull-masked Servant, evades Saber's pursuit, keeping her neither too close nor too far, like a road mirage.

page3.text:
Sparks fly.
Three daggers are hurled without any movement telegraphing their flight. Yet, they fail to touch Saber.

page4.text:
Saber has some resistance to projectile attacks, just as Lancer did.
Compared to Lancer who predicts their trajectories using air current sounds and his opponent's hostile intent,
Saber predicts the attacks using air current sounds and her Intuition.
Invisible attacks are not particularly threatening to Heroic Spirits.
They operate on a level beyond that, killing each other with decisive attacks that may be understood, but not prevented.

page5.text:
To continue the example, Lancer's spear is worthy to be a Heroic Spirit's Noble Phantasm.
It is a weapon that pierces the heart without fail. Even if its identity is known, it cannot be blocked.
The only ways to defend against that demonic spear would be:
to erect a brute barrier with magical energy exceeding that of the spear,
to possess luck so auspicious that it bends the destiny-fixing effect of the spear,
or to prevent Lancer from using the spear to begin with.

page6.text:
Compared to that, Assassin's dirks are easily managed.
They are lethal if they strike a vital point, but the fact that they can be simply blocked makes them little different than pebbles.

page7.text:
"Tch."
Assassin has thrown more than forty dirks.
The robed killer finally stops, his ammunition exhausted.

page8.text:
"Mrgh."
His pursuer skids to a halt as well.
Her enemy, who had kept her at a distance, has suddenly stopped.
She can feel the sinister aura plainly emanating from Assassin.
This is no time for a foolhardy charge.

page9.text:
"Do you accept your fate, Assassin?"
Saber takes a slight step back, despite knowing that the best tactical choice would be to cut him down here.
I must not advance any further.
Her Intuition, which kept her alive for so many years,
broadcasts a warning with maximum urgency.
Do not advance.
Do not approach the gloom.

page10.text:
"Indeed I have, Saber. I am out of ammunition.
And I am prepared to die to a single stroke of your sword, but why do you not approach?"

page11.text:
...
Saber does not answer, but she slightly raises the tip of her sword.
It points at her enemy.
Seven meters separate them now. It would take her two steps to reach him.
It is a range that requires a swordsman like Saber to advance.
Furthermore, she has a hidden weapon she can use only once,
for which range is not even a consideration.

page12.text:
Assassin's black cloak flutters.
He does not know where the breeze stirring it is coming from.

page13.text:
"Hmph. Nothing to say to me? Suit yourself. I'll speak as I please."
The clarity of Assassin's voice belies his appearance.
It resembles someone...the spearman she fought before, perhaps. Saber narrows her eyes.

page14.text:
"But I am impressed you fended them all off. I aimed them so that they would not be seen, but you saw them nonetheless."
"I didn't see them directly, but I can read their trajectories. I could not wield this blade if I feared the unseen."

page15.text:
The skull chuckles in agreement.
What use is throwing black-painted daggers at someone who wields an invisible sword?
Assassin keeps laughing, appreciating the clear difference in the two Heroic Spirits' calibers and the gap in their Noble Phantasms' capabilities.

page16.text:
"So I was never a threat to begin with.
In the end, I am a mere Assassin who cannot stand toe-to-toe with an upstanding Heroic Spirit. We lurk in the shadows. No Heroic Spirit exists to be chosen for such a role."
"What?"

page17.text:
"Thus, all we can do is assassinate. We Assassins are failed imitations of Heroic Spirits who are only able to kill mortal Masters, not Servants.
Thus, I only have one target.
Do you understand now, Saber? Everything I've done has been for the sake of killing your Master."

page18.text:
"Shirou."
"The very same. My lord is entertaining yours.
In drawing me away from him, you've left him to become worm food unless you hurry back soon."
"Guh...!"
Saber's sword flashes into brilliance.
Or rather, she reveals the golden radiance that it always had.

page19.text:
"Ah-ha! So you used a wind charm to conceal the blade. I see now. That gale force could strike me even from there. You don't need to risk yourself by closing in."
The black cloak sinks down.
It turns out that the prey he lured out has a ranged weapon of its own.
No stratagem or calculation can help him now.
If Saber means to cut him from afar, then all Assassin can do is attempt to disrupt her up close.

page20.text:
"Our positions are reversed, Assassin. Will you meet this Barrier of the Wind King?"
"Wicked woman, inviting me to jump into a horde of locusts. And yet, the dragon is about to unleash its breath. What a dilemma..."

page21.text:
The skull mask reaches the ground.
Crouching low, he resembles a crawling spider.
The vacuum vortex of compressed air is about to be unleashed on Assassin.
It would be insane to face it.
Does he really expect to endure that lethal tempest by curling up on the ground?

page22.text:
"Clearly, this will be our final exchange. Allow me to say something first, Saber.
You claimed that you could beat me in a duel."
Saber raises her sword.
She won't let him stall for an escape with words.
Her eyes are locked on to Assassin.
Even if he attempts spatial teleportation, she can finish him before he moves.

page23.text:
"That is why you separated me from him. It was the right decision to protect your Master."
She's raised her sword as high as it will go.
Now, all she has to do is let it fall. Assassin sinks even lower to the floor.

page24.text:
"But, how will you protect yourself, I wonder?"
He asks a question.
To that,
"I must go. Goodbye, Assassin."
Saber answers with her sword.

page25.text:
The duel is decided.
Like a divine dragon, the vortex of air swallows corridor and skull both, snaking through the temple in a violent tumult.

page26.text:
There is no blocking or dodging it.
As with Lancer's spear, the only way to stop Saber's Invisible Air is by overcoming it with sheer magical energy.
Assassin's magical energy can't even compare to Saber's.
The only way he could have stopped the attack is by stopping Saber from unleashing it.

page27.text:
But it's too late to stop the released tempest.
The black cloak is sure to be cut into ribbons within a second of her sword stroke.
A vortex of death descends on him.
But in the midst of that vacuum wave...
"God is great!"
Assassin cries out an exultant laugh, and charges.

page28.text:
"Guh...!"
An attack aimed at her neck.
As Saber instantly parries it, the black cloak slips over her head and drops behind her.

page29.text:
"Damn you!"
With godlike speed, Saber spins to attack him.
But Assassin is no longer there, having leapt out of range.

page30.text:
At the same time...
"Wha..."
The ominous presence she's been feeling now covers the ground beneath her feet.

page31.text:
"It seems you're unlucky on two fronts, Saber."
The shadow spreads.
Its muddy corruption taints her silver armor.

page32.text:
"The first is a matter of compatibility. Those who traverse the desert always call upon a djinn's charm to ward off the wind. It is the only magecraft I know how to invoke."
The corridor is plunged into darkness.
Pale moonlight fails to illuminate the shadows.
As her consciousness fades,
she sees it.

page33.text:
"Assass...in...you..."
"That's right, Saber. Your second misfortune was choosing to fight here. You should have noticed what vile creature was lurking here."

page34.text:
"Ngh...argh..."
She can't even hear Assassin's voice.
In a few more seconds, she will disappear.
This Shadow consumes Servants.
Her body screams in revulsion, even as her thoughts fade.

page35.text:
"...!"
It doesn't matter if it's a futile gesture.
She'll spend every last drop of magical energy, if that's what it takes to break out of this bind.

page36.text:
The Shadow still only covers her feet.
If she fights against it at maximum output, she can break free.
Even if she loses most of her energy and the part of her taken by the Shadow, at least she can escape.

page37.text:
And yet...
"Now, that won't do. You will disappear here, Saber."
The Shadow isn't her only foe.
The skull had been watching this effort play out like a spectator, but he is still a grim reaper here to bring death.

page38.text:
"You...planned...this..."
"You said you would win in a duel. That's certainly true. But you are alone, while I have two on my side. All I had to do was make you lower your guard."
The Shadow encroaches further.

page39.text:
"Nngh...! Argh, agh..."
Her very existence begins to decay, starting with her feet.
She's lost sensation from her toes to her thighs.
Her legs becoming both part of this world, and not part of it.

page40.text:
"A Servant cannot resist that alyal. That's doubly true for a proper Heroic Spirit like you. Even a relatively similar being like me will have its magical energy robbed with a touch. For one as pure as you, its mere touch is enough to lose your sanity.
...Still, it would be a waste to have you disappear. I would fail to fulfill my goal. I will have your heart."

page41.text:
"And how...will you do that?"
"Is that so strange? Do you think I have no way to kill you, just because I am out of daggers and cannot approach the Shadow?"

page42.text:
Murderous intent emanates from the skull.
Assassin's magical energy, which felt feeble so far, concentrates in his right arm.

page43.text:
His right arm is a club,
a misshapen thing without even a hand, that does not function as an arm.
All it can do is dumbly strike his opponent. It cannot even hold his daggers.
Now, it warps.
Bones bend and break. The skull's arm explodes upward like an abominable wing.

page44.text:
What a bizarre sight.
What a long, massive arm.
Where another arm would end in a fist, that is only his elbow.
It bends into a grotesque forearm and hand that seems sewn into his shoulder.

page45.text:
...
Saber's thoughts freeze.
It can reach her.
That arm is long enough to reach her.
Once it does, it is sure to gouge out her heart.
Before she can even tremble, his arm flutters.

page46.text:
The cursed arm is thrust at her like a spear.
There is a sound of flesh being sliced, and a gout of fresh blood.
Red liquid splashes on the floor and speckles the black Shadow.

page47.text:
"Keee!"
A shrill cackle escapes the skull mask.
His outstretched arm is coated in crimson.
Its deed done, it quickly retracts back towards Assassin.
"Kee, keekeekeekeekeekeekeekeekeekee!!!"
He has lost his monstrous arm.

page48.text:
"D-daMn you! whY WOn't You jUST diE!?"
"Haah...hah...ah..."
She lowers her sword.
Assassin's cursed arm never reached Saber.
Saber repelled the curse before it could extract a mirror image of her heart.

page49.text:
Assassin's Noble Phantasm cannot defeat Saber, even in these dire straits.
No...
Having survived Lancer's causality-reversing spear, she won't allow herself to die to such a vulgar curse.

page50.text:
"Argh...ssst..."
But that was the last resistance she can offer.
All the power she built up to resist the Shadow was spent in this final defense.

page51.text:
She has no strength left to struggle with, and even if she did, it would be too late.
The sinister aura she's felt this entire time is now emanating from her very self.
The Shadow devours her feet and reaches for her waist.
Not even moonlight can escape its hunger, and now, it has become her.
It's too late to do anything.

page52.text:
...The Shadow creeps upward.
It clouds over the silver-clad swordswoman's vision.

page53.text:
"I'm sorry...Shi...rou..."
She gasps as if craving oxygen, and sinks into the murky swamp.
